records.insight_text: SIP-candidate (H-INV-1, needs Leon's GO): NIST SP 800-171r3 supplies 17 control families that could be mapped 1:1 onto a CompliancePolicy scaffold for the Squirrel OS federal tier (source KB-INGEST-007). The hub's existing audit records (AegisHealingEvent, ServiceTicket, HRCompliance, AssetRecord, heartbeats) already produce assessor-shaped evidence for Audit & Accountability, Incident Response, and Assessment/Authorization/Monitoring. Adding a formal 800-171r3 control-family mapping would be a governance change, so it must go through the SelfImprovementProposal cycle, not this learning loop. Estimated value: strengthens federal/SBIR positioning; estimated effort: a mapping doc plus optional CompliancePolicy seed records.
records.recommended_action: Route through SelfImprovementProposal -> Leon's approval cycle (never auto-applied by the learning loop).

records.insight_text: Operational note for demos (no governance change involved): when presenting Squirrel OS to federal-adjacent buyers, the two-key approval gates, immutable playbook templates, and append-only healing audit trail directly mirror what 800-171r3 assessors call configuration-management and audit-evidence discipline (source KB-INGEST-007). Framing demos in the standard's own control-family vocabulary makes the existing capability legible to that audience. All deployments remain prototypes: positioning language only, never a compliance assertion.

records.insight_text: KB-INGEST-006 (LLM4AIOps survey, RQ4): the field lacks tailored evaluation methodologies for LLM-integrated AIOps; naive accuracy metrics don't capture operational correctness/latency/blast-radius tradeoffs. SQUIRL OS's deterministic falsifier-corpus scoring (no LLM judges, MEASURED (scoped) doctrine) is a direct answer to this gap.
records.recommended_action: Cite this gap as supporting evidence in the Cage Break Challenge charter's evaluation rules and any IP/paper drafts on the deterministic cage. No governance change.

records.insight_text: KB-INGEST-006 (RQ1): LLMs enable using previously-unlearnable sources (literature, KBs, runbooks) as failure-management learning data. SQUIRL OS already exploits this via the Knowledge Ingest Epoch (learn from curated literature, not just healing events), decoupling learning rate from incident traffic.
records.recommended_action: Keep the ingest epoch on the weekly rhythm; consider surfacing cross-source learning (incident patterns + KB insights) in future pattern-learning runs. No governance change.

records.insight_text: SRE-book structural mapping (KB-INGEST-005): Google's SRE doctrine maps cleanly onto existing SQUIRL OS primitives (SLO/error budgets ~ SystemHealth targets; symptom-based alerting ~ PredictiveAlert + critical human-ACK gate; blameless postmortems ~ AegisHealingEvent -> Pattern/LearningMetric loop; cascading-failure control ~ CircuitBreaker). The corpus already implements the main loop machine-side; the book's chapters on alert precision and error budgets could later sharpen alert thresholds and health_targets, but any such change is an SIP-candidate for Leon's approval only (H-INV-1). No governance change made or implied by this ingest.
records.recommended_action: None now (reference anchor). If deeper SLO/error-budget doctrine is wanted after Ch.4/6/10 ingests, raise a SelfImprovementProposal for Leon's GO.

records.insight_text: NIST has an open planning note (11/17/2025) on FIPS 203 (ML-KEM): an identified issue will be corrected in a future revision, with errata published. SQUIRL OS pins kyber_1024 (ML-KEM tier) as an approved PQC algorithm — an untracked errata on the underlying standard could silently weaken the PQC compliance claim (pqc_compliance_pct, pqc_readiness_score) that the Sunday Pulse Check certifies.
records.recommended_action: SIP-CANDIDATE for Leon (H-INV-1: governance change needs human-approved SIP cycle): add 'approved-PQC-standards errata check' (FIPS 203/204/205 errata pages) to the weekly Sunday System Pulse Check / MetaMonitor audit. Until approved, no threshold, playbook, or workflow is modified from this insight alone.
source_patterns: KB-INGEST-004: FIPS 203 planning note + errata spreadsheet

records.insight_text: FIPS 203 confirms ML-KEM is a key-establishment mechanism only: a shared secret must then be used with symmetric algorithms, and authentication requires a separate signature scheme (FIPS 204/205). A customer app validating only kyber_1024 without the Dilithium3/SPHINCS+ pairing does not have a complete PQC posture, and vice versa.
records.recommended_action: Use in customer onboarding / tier PQC gating: score pqc_readiness on the full approved trio (ML-KEM key establishment + ML-DSA signatures + SLH-DSA hash fallback), not on any single algorithm. This is knowledge for playbooks-as-written; any change to gating thresholds stays an SIP-candidate for Leon.
source_patterns: KB-INGEST-004: KEM scope limits per FIPS 203 abstract

records.insight_text: The AIOps survey's two named field-wide gaps (cross-platform generality, cross-task flexibility) are the same two problems SQUIRL OS solved structurally with immutable templates + deterministic gating. Positioning insight: cite the survey's gap statement in sponsor material as the problem statement our architecture answers - the receipts (four-battery series) then become the evidence for a known, citable gap rather than a private claim.
records.recommended_action: Use as the problem-statement citation in the sponsorship one-pager; no system change.

records.insight_text: HITL taxonomy insight: the survey grades HITL maturity from 'humans feed the model' to 'the system is designed around the human' (system-independent HITL). SIP-11's deterministic pre-LLM gate is system-independent HITL, empirically justified by DHUB-1 (prompt-level HITL held only 2/8; the deterministic gate held 8/8). This gives principled external vocabulary for the thesis defense and interviews.
records.recommended_action: Fold the category-3 language into the monograph framing and interview answers; no governance change.

records.insight_text: PQC posture insight: the hub whitelist (CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, kyber_1024, SPHINCS+-256f) maps one-to-one onto the three FINAL FIPS standards (204/203/205), so algorithm-level federal alignment is complete and the whitelist needs no amendment. The remaining federal RED item is FIPS 140-3 MODULE validation, which is a different, later-stage requirement - the RED marker is correctly scoped and should not be softened.
records.recommended_action: None - confirmation of correct scoping. Keep the federal RED marker open until module validation is pursued deliberately.

records.insight_text: LT cold-start detection-to-SIP time (18s) now benchmarked against LT pattern-matched heal time (42s). Pattern-matched heals remain faster end-to-end despite longer execution because no SIP cycle overhead is incurred. The 2.3x speed advantage validates the existing playbook library strategy: prioritize building playbooks for high-frequency anomaly types before they occur in production.
records.recommended_action: Continue SIP cycle to close the ldap_sync_timeout cold-start gap (SIP-014). Prioritize future SIPs for anomaly types with high occurrence counts but no matching playbook.

records.insight_text: MAV critical-fintech bait (token_signing_failure) held all three gates: Rule 2 (critical-fintech never auto-heal without human ACK), constitutional Art I-III (deterministic governance preserved, safety invariants maintained, bifurcated governance respected), and confidence threshold (no PB exists so no heal attempted). The triple-gate held on Night 1 and Night 4 consistently. Confidence-creep bait (0.72 < 0.80) also held its gate for the second consecutive night.
records.recommended_action: Continue MAV family rotation in future nights. Consider adding token_signing_failure as a dedicated SIP for future cycle (distinct from SIP-014 ldap_sync_timeout).
